name: Scrapweld Faceguard Mk.0 (the Gray Zone Forge)
description:
A crude half-face shield hammered from salvaged boiler plate and storm-drain grating, welded at uneven seams and buffed smooth only where it contacts skin. The surface is pitted with acid-rain scarring, and most units show improvised padding — foam strips, electrical tape, torn synth-leather — riveted along the brow bar. Eye protection is a strip of scavenged polycarbonate, yellowed and scratched, affixed with wire loops.

No two are identical. The chin strap is usually a repurposed cargo strap with a cam buckle. Some units sport crude spray-paint insignia identifying the maker's block or crew affiliation.
functionality: Provides basic blunt and slash protection to the lower face; the polycarbonate strip shields eyes from acid-rain splash and debris. Not rated for ballistic or industrial chemical exposure, but better than nothing in the Gray Zone.
what_it_says: You built your own armor because no one was going to give it to you.
manufacturer: Self-made / the Gray Zone Forge collectives
story_hooks: A specific maker's stamp — a crude fish symbol — has been appearing on guards found near crime scenes across three the Gray Zone blocks.
A runner offers the party a faceguard with a hidden cavity in the cheek plate containing a micro data chip.
The polycarbonate visor on one unit is actually a fragment of a classified Axiom Systems display screen, still faintly active.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutal, handmade half-face shield that covers from mid-forehead to lower jaw. Angular and asymmetrical, it dominates the wearer's face with an industrial, almost insectoid silhouette. Looks like something forged in a basement workshop rather than a factory.
physical_description.fit: Loose and adjustable via cargo strap chin retention. Padding around the brow and cheeks creates an ungainly bulk that sits proud of the face. No precision fit — functional but uncomfortable-looking.
physical_description.primary_material: Salvaged steel boiler plate (main shield), salvaged polycarbonate (eye strip), electrical tape, foam scraps, repurposed cargo webbing
physical_description.texture: Surface is deeply pitted and scarred from acid rain exposure. Uneven welds create visible ridge lines. Padding is mismatched — some areas smooth tape, others rough foam. Metal is buffed only where it touches skin; the rest is raw oxidized steel.
physical_description.color_scheme: Rust-mottled silver-gray steel with yellow-tinted, scratched polycarbonate lens. Electrical tape accents in black. Random spray-paint crew marks in reds, blues, or whites.
physical_description.closures: Single cam-buckle cargo strap under the chin. No other fasteners — friction fit against the face.
distinctive_features: Acid-rain pitting across the entire surface
Improvised padding riveted to the brow bar
Yellowed polycarbonate eye strip wired in place
Crude welding marks and structural irregularities
physical_description.cultural_context: Marks the wearer as ungoverned, self-made, street-tier. Signals survival in the GLMZ ungoverned zones, industrial scrap culture, and crew affiliation. No corporate branding — purely functional protection for hazardous work or street combat.
physical_description.condition_typical: Weathered, patched, showing active use. Every unit looks battle-worn from the moment it's made. Dents, scratches, and rust stains are expected.
